question.problem: Find $\dfrac{\partial f}{\partial y}$ given that $f(x,y) = 3x\ln y + 2ye^x.$
question.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $y,$ treating all other variables as constants.

Additionally, we use the sum and constant multiple rules for differentiation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3x\operatorname{ln}⁡y+2y{e}^{x}) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3x\operatorname{ln}⁡y)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y{e}^{x}) \\  & =3x\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y)+2{e}^{x}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂y}(y) \\  & =3x\cdot \frac{1}{y}+2{e}^{x}\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{3x}{y}+2{e}^{x}\end{aligned}
$$
